summary_md: A design review dated 2026-09-24, filed as Paul's research note, of the Astra brief that became the Mentat sector growth study. It estimates nothing. Its core advice: make prior-year real growth the main question and fit log spending on sector and year fixed effects plus lagged raw percent growth (g(t-1)), separately for organizational PAC giving and LDA lobbying, never summed. Treat election expectations as a separate, exploratory study, because more sectors do not create more elections (about 9 elections, 6 chamber flips). It also says three of the brief's specifications do not test their hypotheses: a contraction dummy is not an asymmetric slope (use g+ and g-); Shift = P - M plus current control only reparameterizes P plus M; and a unified-government term cannot separate expected from current control. On data, it says not to fill missing control probabilities with realized results. It says 538 models that use fundraising create a feedback loop, so a polls-only sensitivity is better. It warns that LDA in-house totals already include retained-firm payments and association dues. With five sectors, it says, use the restricted wild-cluster bootstrap and leave-one-sector-out checks. Against the system as built, several points were adopted: raw percent growth, g_pos/g_neg splits, the restricted wild-cluster bootstrap with a few-cluster guard, LOSO/LOYO, the 538 Lite seat forecasts, and lobbying series that are never summed. Others were not. The primary models use dollar levels with national phase and expected-control controls, and year fixed effects and logs are only robustness checks. The giving outcome is Mentat general giving across all recipient types. The 2023/2025 expected control was filled after the fact by Paul's ruling. The later Codex audit vindicated the review's main warning: the L3-LV lobbying slope of +0.352 flipped to -0.477 under sector and year fixed effects (UNSTRATIFIED, 5 sectors, 2008-2023).

bearings.paper_claim: Main model should be log S_it = alpha_i + lambda_t + beta g_(i,t-1): sector effects plus full year effects (which absorb odd/even and presidential/midterm patterns), raw percent growth, log dollars; dynamic and other terms only as sensitivities.
bearings.paper_location: A simple formula to start with; sections 1, 3, 13; design step 4
bearings.system_side: Built core models fit dollar LEVELS ($M 2025) on sector FE plus national controls pres_year, midterm_year, exp_dem_house/senate (plus cur_dem for lobbying); sector+year FE and ln(DV) exist only as ROBUSTNESS variants (R-yearFE, R-log, R-logFE). Codex audit 2026-09-26: L3-LV +0.352 flips to -0.477 with sector+year FE, log-FE -0.006, adj R2 0.884717 vs 0.884690 (5 sectors, 2008-2023, UNSTRATIFIED).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies directly: same study, same panel. The review predates the build by one day; Paul's rulings R1-R9 approved the staged plan built on the brief, so promoting the year-FE log model to primary is Paul's call.

bearings.paper_claim: A contraction indicator estimates a level jump at zero, not an asymmetric slope; define contraction on raw growth below 0 and use g+ = max(g,0), g- = max(-g,0) with separate coefficients.
bearings.system_side: ASYM splits each growth variable into g_pos = max(g,0) and g_neg = min(g,0) with a bootstrap equality test; CONTRACT-a/b keep 1(g<0) but label it a level shift. Contraction is defined on raw pct growth, not a z-score. Sign convention differs: built g_neg is non-positive, so the distress hypothesis predicts a NEGATIVE slope.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct. Readers must flip the sign when comparing the built g_neg slope to the review's g- coefficient.

bearings.paper_claim: f(P-M)+gM = fP+(g-f)M: Shift adds no information beyond P and current control M; a test of current versus expected power needs both terms in the model.
bearings.system_side: exp_shift = exp_dem - cur_dem is built per chamber; the code notes it reparametrises the lobbying model (cur_dem retained), but the contribution core controls (SGS_C_CONTROLS) carry exp_dem and no cur_dem, so H4shift-C swaps in a restricted contrast rather than testing P and M jointly. SHIFT preview found no stable partisan shift (-0.04, p .76, 2021-25, chamber-stacked).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds whenever a year-level probability is entered with or without current control; within-chamber year FE would absorb both anyway.

bearings.paper_claim: Main campaign outcome should be corporate/trade-association PAC disbursements to congressional candidates; individual, party, super PAC and IE channels separate; never combine donor-to-PAC receipts with PAC-to-candidate payments; SSF budgets are not sponsor profits.
bearings.system_side: Ruling R4 sets contributions = Mentat general giving across all recipient categories, and the 2026-09-26 ruling keeps non_giving receipts (e.g. Stripe 464K to NRSC 2021-22) in every test; workbook 08 found only 5.6% of dollars reach House/Senate candidates; gifts to company PACs = 8.84% of 2021-25 giving (overlap check added).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paul's rulings govern scope; the review's point bears on interpreting C1-C3 as a capacity mechanism, not on whether the series is collected.

bearings.paper_claim: With five to ten sectors, report small-sample cluster corrections, restricted wild-cluster inference, cluster leverage and leave-one-sector-out; bootstrap p-values are not a guarantee; Driscoll-Kraay only as sensitivity with about 18 years.
bearings.system_side: Every focal term uses a wild cluster restricted bootstrap-t with Webb six-point weights; with G sectors the code prints that p below 2/6^G is unreachable and marks the term descriptive; STRATIFIED/UNSTRATIFIED labels; LOSO and LOYO variants. No Driscoll-Kraay seen in sgs_estimate.R, although the transcribed original contract asks for it.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct; the review's ceiling (no method repairs few independent units) applies to every pooled growth coefficient.

bearings.paper_claim: Some 538 models use fundraising, so explaining contributions with them creates a feedback problem; prefer polls-only. More monthly rows improve timing resolution, not the number of independent elections (about 9 elections, 6 flips): exploratory.
bearings.system_side: SEATS-W uses 538 Lite as primary precisely because it leaves out the Classic/Deluxe fundraising fundamentals (code notes Lite is not strictly polls-only), as-of gated; the -3.47 pp D share per expected D seat (House 2022, 17 weeks, block-bootstrap p .0086-.0174) is labelled one election and EXPLORATORY.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds until 2018/2020 weekly money joins; even then independent elections stay few.

bearings.paper_claim: Value added, gross output/revenue, profits and assets are different quantities; output growth is not spare cash; corporate PAC budgets come from voluntary SSF contributions, so a capacity mechanism fits lobbying more than PAC giving.
bearings.paper_location: Overall verdict risk 1; sections 2 and 10; BEA definitions paragraph
bearings.system_side: The cycle model's 50/50 budget term uses the IBISWorld REAL annual revenue growth path with a one-year lag; D-116 (2026-10-08) already dropped the 50/50 for company PACs (x = 0), leaving it on other measures.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Bears on any measure where revenue growth stands in for a giving budget; the sector-study backtest (naive MAE 3.63 vs +growth 3.99, LobbyView 2014-2023) is consistent with a weak revenue-to-spending link.

bearings.paper_claim: LDA in-house expenses include retained-firm payments and lobbying-related association dues, so adding client expenses, firm revenues and association expenses double-counts; keep the series separate or deduplicate.
bearings.system_side: Mentat shows LDA in-house and outside-firm lobbying side by side and states they are never summed; the sector study keeps outside-firm income and self-filer expenses as separate DVs.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct for any sector total; trade-association overlap is not yet handled separately in either surface.

gaps_exposed: No primary sector+year-FE log-dollar growth model: year FE and logs exist only as robustness variants, though the Codex audit showed the lobbying slope flips sign under them.
Contribution core models carry expected control without current control, so H4 cannot compare current versus expected power for giving.
Expected control for 2023 and 2025 is post-period (Crystal Ball Nov-2024 call, Sep-2026 snapshot); no available_at gate in the main spec.
Trade-association LDA spending is not reported separately or overlap-adjusted; issue-code dollars must not be split across topics.
No count of active contributors/clients or concentration measure to separate participation changes from per-actor spending.
No policy-salience proxy (lagged hearing counts or Unified Agenda proceedings) in the built specs.
Driscoll-Kraay sensitivity named in the transcribed original contract is not visible in sgs_estimate.R.
flags: Conflict with Paul's ruling (2026-09-25 ~19:40, reversing 1a): the review says not to fill unavailable control probabilities with results or later information; the built 2023 value uses the Nov-2024 Crystal Ball call. Paul's ruling governs; label those rows retrospective.

Conflict with Paul's rulings R4 and Keep those receipts: the review wants organizational PAC-to-candidate giving as the main outcome; the built outcome is all-recipient general giving including non-giving receipts.
Authorship: the text reviews the Astra brief and reads as an external (likely AI) reviewer's output filed under Paul's name; treat its recommendations as advice, not Paul's rulings.
The review estimates nothing; any claim that it validates or refutes the growth effect is UNVERIFIED (DE-062). Its 3.05 percent figure is an illustration for beta = 0.03, not a result.
Pooled growth coefficients quoted here (L3-LV +0.352 / -0.477) span 5 sectors with no sector-only estimates: UNSTRATIFIED.
LDA is used here as a spending outcome only, never an edge or weight source (D-021).
paul_alignment: No annotated-bibliography entry exists for this note. Paul's recorded position on the study (returns literature, deep-pockets reading) and his early 'seems to confirm' reading of the lobbying result are not supported by this review, which predicts no sign, or by the later year-FE check, where the slope flipped. The note is partly stale relative to the system: the build adopted raw percent growth, g_pos/g_neg, a few-cluster wild bootstrap, LOSO/LOYO, Lite seat forecasts and never-summed lobbying. Its main-spec, outcome-scope and no-post-period-fill advice was overridden or left as robustness, and those choices still stand.

related.why: Both bear on the sector+year fixed-effects design; Imai and Kim caution what two-way FE identifies, while the review makes it the primary specification.
Low overlap between organizational lobbying and PAC spending supports the review's rule to model PAC giving and lobbying separately and never sum them.
Cited for the deep-pockets/returns motivation of the growth hypothesis that the review reframes as capacity versus distress versus policy exposure.
Links lobbying and PACs to market concentration; the review asks for concentration and active-actor counts to separate participation from spending.
Documents election-cycle synchronization of lobbying, the phase pattern the review absorbs with full year effects and that the built model handles with pres/midterm controls.
Paul's cross-industry LDA report uses the same LD-2 filings whose in-house versus outside-firm accounting the review warns can double count.
